transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Yeah, so... I guess I'm here because for almost two years now, I just haven't been able to shake this absolute certainty about my ensemble. Ever since this big commission I had, a few people in the group started quietly undermining my work. They do it through, like, sudden schedule changes and messing with the seating choices. 

Which, honestly, seating is such a delicate science. You wouldn't believe how much moving the cellos just two feet to the left can completely ruin the acoustic balance of a piece. I actually spent a whole semester in grad school just studying the reverberation of different wood types in 19th-century European concert halls. It’s fascinating stuff, really. I always thought if I wasn't composing and directing, I'd probably be an acoustic engineer. Or maybe an architect. I love the way old buildings smell, you know? Like dust and history. 

But, um... sorry, what was I saying? Right, the ensemble. So they do the seating thing, and they make these little comments during rehearsals. And the thing is, even when they try to show me emails or rehearsal notes that supposedly explain why they made the changes, I know what they're actually doing. They're trying to sabotage the performance, and it's just impossible to ignore anymore.
Do you believe that the people in your ensemble are intentionally trying to harm your career or reputation?

Yeah, exactly. Like I was just saying, it's definitely intentional. They want to ruin my reputation, especially after that big commission. I mean, they'll wave these printed-out emails in my face, or point to the rehearsal notes to try and justify why they pushed the schedule back or messed with the seating again, but I know it's just a cover to undermine my work. It's so obvious. 

And speaking of the emails, actually, the whole ensemble mailing list has been a nightmare lately because the server keeps bouncing messages. I had to talk to the IT guy—Greg, I think his name is?—and he was going on and on about server migrations. I actually built my own PC last year for audio mixing, so I know a bit about it. I put in a custom liquid cooling loop. Took me, like, three weeks to bend the tubing perfectly so it wouldn't leak all over the motherboard. You really need a powerhouse machine if you're running full orchestral sample libraries. I had to get 128 gigs of RAM just to load the brass section without the whole program crashing. It's a really expensive setup, honestly, but the rendering speeds are incredible. 

Wait, sorry. What were we talking about? Oh, right, the ensemble. But yeah, to answer your question, they are definitely trying to sabotage my career.
Can you explain how you know for sure that the ensemble is trying to sabotage your work, even when they provide explanations for their actions?

Well, I just... I know it. It's this absolute certainty I've had for almost two years now. Ever since I got that big commission, it's just been so clear that a few people in the group are using these subtle things to quietly undermine me. The schedule changes, the little comments during rehearsals... 

And the seating choices, like I mentioned. It's really insidious because they try to pass it off as logistical stuff. They'll literally pull up these emails or rehearsal notes and be like, "Oh, we had to move the violas because of the lighting rig," or whatever. But I know what it really is. 

Actually, speaking of lighting rigs, the venue we were playing at last month had these awful halogen spots. They run so hot. I was sweating through my shirt halfway through the first movement. I actually read this article recently about how LED stage lighting is completely changing theater design because you don't have to account for the massive heat output anymore. It's crazy how much energy those old lights waste. I was talking to my friend Sarah about it—she does set design for a local theater company—and she said they just switched their entire grid to LEDs and their electric bill dropped by like forty percent. Which makes sense, right? Plus you get all those programmable RGB options, so you can change the mood of a scene with just a tablet. I kind of wish I had a setup like that in my apartment, just to mess around with. 

Anyway... what was the question? Oh, how do I know for sure. Yeah, it's just... even with their so-called explanations, the emails and the notes, I just know they're using all of it to sabotage me. It's been going on for two years, and you just don't shake a certainty like that.

You mentioned that others show you emails or rehearsal notes to explain their actions, but you still believe they are trying to sabotage you. Have you ever considered that their explanations might be genuine, or does that idea not seem possible to you at all?

Honestly, no, it really doesn't seem possible. I know they show me those emails and notes, but... I mean, for almost two years now, ever since that commission, I've just had this absolute certainty. They are quietly undermining my work with the schedule changes, the seating choices, the little comments. It's not genuine. 

And you know, speaking of genuine things, I went to this antique market over the weekend trying to find a genuine metronome from the 1920s. The craftsmanship back then was just unreal. They used solid mahogany and actual brass fittings. I found one guy selling a Seth Thomas model, but he had clearly replaced the pendulum bob with a cheap piece of plastic. Which is just insulting, really. If you're going to restore a vintage piece, you have to source the right materials. I actually took a woodworking class a few summers ago just so I could learn how to properly restore the veneer on this old upright piano I found on Craigslist. It took me three months just to strip the old finish off without damaging the wood underneath. The fumes from the stripper were awful, though. I had to buy a heavy-duty respirator, which made me look like I was walking around in a sci-fi movie. 

Wait, sorry, I'm drifting again. Um... but yeah, no, their explanations aren't genuine. I've been unable to shake this certainty for two years. They are definitely trying to sabotage me.
Have you ever thought that maybe you're misinterpreting their actions, even slightly, or do you feel completely certain—without any doubt—that they are plotting against you?

I mean... no. I haven't really thought I'm misinterpreting it. Like I said, I'm here because for almost two years I've been unable to shake this certainty. After I got that commission, it just started happening. A few people in the ensemble using schedule changes, seating choices, those little comments in rehearsals... they're quietly undermining my work. And even when they show me those emails or notes that supposedly explain it, I know what's really going on. 

It's kind of like... well, speaking of notes, I was actually looking at some original manuscript copies of Beethoven's Fifth the other day online. It's fascinating how messy his handwriting was. You can literally see where he crossed things out so violently the quill almost tore the paper. I actually bought a set of calligraphy pens last month because I thought it would be cool to hand-write my scores. It is incredibly difficult. I ended up with ink all over my hands. It took three days of scrubbing with pumice soap to get the black stains out of my cuticles. Which is a problem when you're directing, because everyone is looking at your hands. I had this one rehearsal where the principal cellist couldn't stop staring at my fingers, and I had to stop and explain that I wasn't turning into a squid or something. 

But, uh, yeah. To answer your question... no, I don't think I'm misinterpreting it at all. I'm completely certain they're plotting against me.

Have you ever had the experience where, even when someone shows you clear proof that contradicts your belief about the ensemble, you still can't accept it and continue to believe they are out to sabotage you?

Yeah, I mean, I feel like I keep saying the same thing, but yes. Even when they bring out their clear proof, like the emails or the rehearsal notes that supposedly explain why they did what they did, I just can't accept it. I'm here because for almost two years now, right after I got that commission, I've been totally unable to shake this certainty. A few people in the ensemble are definitely using those schedule changes, the seating choices, and the little comments in rehearsals to quietly undermine my work. 

Speaking of printing out notes and emails, though, I actually had to buy a new laser printer last week. My old inkjet kept smudging the bar lines on my scores, which is just a nightmare when you're trying to read a complex polyrhythm and the ink is just a giant black blur. I ended up going down this massive internet rabbit hole about the history of printing. Did you know Gutenberg didn't actually invent the first movable type? It was invented in China like four hundred years earlier using porcelain. Porcelain! Can you imagine trying to carve tiny little characters out of clay and baking them without them shrinking or cracking? I took a ceramics class in undergrad as an elective, and I couldn't even make a simple bowl that didn't look like a lopsided ashtray. The kiln we used was so temperamental. You had to monitor the temperature constantly or the glaze would bubble up and ruin hours of work. 

Anyway... sorry, I lost my train of thought. What did you ask? Right, the proof they show me. Yeah. No matter what paperwork they put in front of me, I just know they're undermining me. I can't just turn off what I know is happening.
Have you experienced any other situations where you've had strong beliefs about things others claim aren't true, even if they tried to show you proof otherwise?

Um... no, not really. I don't think so. It's just this one thing with the ensemble. I've never really had any other beliefs like that, where people are trying to prove me wrong about something else. It's really just the sabotage with my work. 

Although, speaking of people trying to prove things, I got into this ridiculous argument with the barista at my local coffee shop the other day about the origin of the flat white. He was absolutely convinced it was invented in Australia, but I read this whole article a while back that traced the exact style of microfoam back to New Zealand in the late 80s. I even pulled up the article on my phone to show him, but he just waved me off because he had a line of customers. Which, fine, I get it, you have to keep the line moving. I used to work in food service during college—I was a host at this overly trendy tapas place downtown. The lighting was so dim you practically needed a flashlight to read the menu, and people were always complaining about the portion sizes. I remember this one couple ordered the patatas bravas and then got furious when it came out in a tiny little ramekin. They demanded to see the manager, who ended up giving them a free pitcher of sangria just to get them to stop yelling. The sangria there was actually really good, though. They soaked the fruit in brandy overnight before mixing it. 

But, uh... wait. Did that answer your question? You were asking if I have other beliefs like this one, right? Yeah, no, it's just the stuff with the ensemble. Nothing else.
Have you ever confronted anyone in the ensemble about your belief that they're trying to sabotage you, or taken any steps to try to stop what you believe they're doing?

Well, um, confronted them? Not directly, no. I haven't like, cornered anyone in the hallway or yelled at them. I just try to work around it, you know? I double-check the schedules myself, I make sure my scores are locked up. 

Speaking of locking things up, I actually had to change the padlock on my gym locker recently. The old combination lock just completely jammed on me. I was standing there in a wet towel for like twenty minutes trying to get it open. I ended up having to get the front desk guy to come back with bolt cutters. It was so embarrassing. He had this massive pair of yellow bolt cutters, they looked like something you'd use to break into a bank vault. Have you ever watched those videos online where people pick locks? It's wild how easy it is to bypass most commercial locks. They just use these tiny little tension wrenches and a rake pick, and they're in within seconds. It kind of makes you wonder why we even bother locking our doors at night. I actually bought a deadbolt for my apartment last year that's supposed to be bump-proof, but after watching those videos, I'm pretty sure a determined teenager with a paperclip could probably get in. 

But anyway... no, I haven't really confronted the ensemble members. I just try to protect my work the best I can.
Have you ever had beliefs that others were trying to harm or deceive you outside of your work with the ensemble?

No, not really. It's strictly about the ensemble and my work. I don't walk around thinking the mailman is reading my letters or that my landlord is spying on me. 

Although, my landlord did send this really weird email last week about "water conservation efforts" and how we all need to take shorter showers. Which is hilarious, because the water pressure in my building is so terrible you can barely get the shampoo out of your hair anyway. I ended up buying one of those high-pressure showerheads off Amazon to try and fix it. It has like, mineral beads inside the handle that are supposedly meant to soften the water? I don't know if the beads actually do anything, but they make this rattling sound every time I turn the water on, kind of like a maraca. I actually used to play the maracas in this Latin jazz band in high school. We were terrible. We tried to cover "Oye Como Va" at the spring talent show and our bass player completely lost the groove in the middle of the solo section. It was just a trainwreck of syncopation. 

Wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, outside of work. No, no. Nobody else is trying to harm me or deceive me. It's just the ensemble stuff.
Have you ever had a belief that you were absolutely certain was true, even though others told you it wasn’t, outside of this situation with the ensemble?

No, I haven't. Like I said, it's really just the ensemble. I don't have any other grand theories or anything like that. I'm pretty grounded, usually.

Well, except for my sense of direction, which is completely non-existent. I am notoriously bad at navigating. I still use GPS to get to the grocery store sometimes, and I've lived in my apartment for three years. The other day, I was trying to find this new synthesizer repair shop—because my vintage Roland Juno-106 started making this awful hissing noise on the chorus effect, which is like the whole reason you buy a Juno in the first place—and the maps app took me down this total dead-end alley behind a strip mall. There was just a dumpster and this huge flock of pigeons. Have you ever noticed how pigeons bob their heads when they walk? I read once that it's to stabilize their vision, because they can't move their eyes like we do. It's like built-in image stabilization. My cousin bought this fancy camera last year with optical image stabilization because he wanted to start a vlog about restoring antique furniture, but he gave up after two weeks because sanding wood is incredibly tedious. He ended up selling the camera on eBay for half of what he paid for it. 

But, uh, no. I don't have any other beliefs like that. Just the ensemble trying to mess with my career. That's it.
Have you ever had a belief that was completely certain to you, even when others showed you clear evidence that it wasn’t true, outside of anything related to your work or the ensemble?

No, definitely not. If someone shows me clear evidence of something, I believe them. I'm a pretty logical person, honestly. Like, I used to think vinyl records objectively sounded better than digital audio, but then my audio engineering professor in grad school did this blind test with us. He played a high-resolution digital file and a pristine vinyl pressing, and literally none of us could tell the difference. It totally blew my mind. 

Speaking of vinyl, I was at this record store downtown last weekend, the one that smells like dust and old patchouli? I was digging through the dollar bin and found an original pressing of this obscure seventies Japanese ambient album. The cover art was just incredible, it had these neon geometric shapes that looked like an old arcade machine. I used to be obsessed with arcade games when I was a kid. There was this pizza place near my house that had a vintage cabinet, and I spent an entire summer trying to beat the high score. I ate so much greasy pepperoni pizza that summer I actually made myself sick. The grease would get all over the joystick, which is incredibly gross to think about now with all the germs and everything. 

But um, yeah, I don't ignore facts. If it's not about the ensemble, I'm completely rational. I don't have any other weird beliefs that I hold onto like that.

Have you ever had a belief that you were absolutely certain was true, even though it wasn’t based in reality and others tried to show you otherwise, outside of anything related to the ensemble or your work?

No, I don't think so. I really don't. Like I said, I'm pretty logical about everything else. If something isn't real, I know it's not real. 

Like, okay, I used to think I could fix anything around my apartment myself, right? Because I grew up watching my dad fix the lawnmower and the plumbing and all that. He had this massive red toolbox that weighed like fifty pounds. So last month, my toaster broke. The lever just wouldn't stay down. I figured, how hard can it be? It's a toaster. I took the whole thing apart on my kitchen counter. There were so many crumbs. Just an unbelievable amount of burnt toast dust everywhere. And then I realized I had no idea what any of the internal wiring actually did. I tried to put it back together and ended up with three extra screws. I eventually just threw it out and bought a new one at Target. While I was there, I ended up buying this ridiculous oversized fleece blanket that looks like a giant tortilla. It's actually incredibly comfortable, especially when I'm sitting at my desk trying to score string arrangements late at night. The strings can be so tricky to balance, you know? If the cellos are too heavy, it just muddies the whole mix... 

But, right, sorry. No, I don't have any beliefs like that. Just the stuff with the ensemble. That's the only thing.
Have you ever had a belief that was completely certain to you, even though it wasn’t based in reality and others tried to show you otherwise, outside of anything related to the ensemble or your work?

No, really, I haven't. I feel like I keep saying the same thing, but it's true. Outside of the ensemble thing, I'm just a normal, rational guy. 

I mean, I guess I used to believe that I was going to be a professional skateboarder when I was like, twelve. I was absolutely certain of it. I made my mom drive me to the skatepark every single weekend. I had this deck with this crazy alien graphic on it, and I put these bright green wheels on it. I spent months trying to learn how to kickflip in my driveway, and I just kept destroying my shins. The grip tape would literally scrape the skin right off. Eventually, I realized I had terrible balance and zero coordination, so I gave it up and started playing piano instead. Which honestly worked out way better for me, because I hate being outside when it's hot. The humidity just wrecks my hair, and sweating is the worst. I don't understand people who run marathons for fun. Like, you're just paying money to be exhausted and sweaty for hours. My neighbor runs marathons, and she's always leaving these muddy running shoes in the hallway outside her door...

But yeah, no. I don't have any delusions or weird beliefs or anything. Just the stuff I've been telling you about the ensemble.
Have you ever had a belief that others tried to correct or disprove, where you remained completely certain it was true, even though it wasn't based in reality?

Well, if you're including the ensemble now, then yeah, that's exactly why I'm here. I mean, I've been saying that's the only thing. For almost two years now, right after we got that big commission, I've had this absolute certainty that a few people in the group are quietly trying to undermine my work. 

They do it through these sudden schedule changes, or weird seating choices... which, honestly, the seating in our rehearsal space is a nightmare anyway. We have these horrible metal folding chairs that squeak every time someone even breathes. I don't know how the brass section deals with it. I actually tried to get the venue manager to upgrade them last fall, but he’s this super grumpy guy who always wears these faded Hawaiian shirts, even in December. It’s freezing in that hall, and he’s walking around looking like he’s on his way to a luau. I think he buys them at thrift stores, because one of them had a stain on the pocket that looked exactly like Dijon mustard. I put mustard on everything, by the way. Sandwiches, pretzels, sometimes even eggs if I'm feeling crazy... 

But anyway, yeah, they use the seating arrangements and these little comments during rehearsals to sabotage my pieces. And they try to disprove it to me, you know? They’ll show me emails or forward me these administrative notes that supposedly explain why the schedule shifted or why they said what they said, but I know what's really going on. I just can't shake the certainty of it, no matter what they show me.
Have you ever had a belief that you were absolutely certain was true, even though others showed you clear evidence that it wasn't, outside of anything related to your work or the ensemble?

No, I really haven't. I feel like we're just going in circles here, but honestly, outside of the ensemble, there's nothing. I'm totally grounded. 

I mean, the closest thing to a "false belief" I've had lately was thinking I could keep a fern alive in my apartment. I bought this beautiful Boston fern at the farmer's market a few months ago. The guy selling it swore it was low maintenance, and he had this really cool vintage truck he was selling out of—like, an old Ford from the sixties, painted this perfect robin's egg blue. I've always wanted a classic car, but parking in the city is just impossible. You have to move your car for street cleaning twice a week, and the tickets are outrageous. My buddy Dave got three tickets in one month and ended up having to sell his car. He bought an electric scooter instead, which is terrifying because he weaves in and out of traffic like a maniac. I tried riding it once and almost crashed into a mail truck. The mail carrier was so mad, she actually yelled at me. Which I guess is fair, but still...

Anyway, the fern died in like three weeks. Totally brown and crispy. But no, to answer your question, no other beliefs like that. Just the situation with the ensemble.
Have you ever had a belief that you were absolutely certain was true, even when others showed you clear evidence that it wasn't, outside of anything related to your work or the ensemble?

Look, I feel like you're asking me the exact same thing again, and the answer is still no. Outside of the ensemble, my life is completely normal. I don't have any strange beliefs or... delusions, or whatever you want to call it. 

I really don't know how else to explain it. I'm a pretty rational person. Like, I'm the guy who organizes the spreadsheets for our grocery runs. My roommate, Mark, is terrible at grocery shopping. He always goes when he's hungry and comes back with, like, three boxes of off-brand cereal and zero actual food. Last week he bought this giant tub of generic cheese puffs that tasted like cardboard and sadness. We ended up leaving it on the counter for days until we finally threw it out because we saw a moth near it. Pantry moths are the worst, by the way. Once they get into your flour, you basically have to throw out your entire kitchen. My aunt had an infestation a few years ago, and she spent hundreds of dollars on these weird pheromone traps. She’s kind of eccentric anyway, she collects those ceramic frogs and puts them all over her garden. But yeah, no, I don't have any other beliefs like that. Just the stuff with the musicians.

Can you think of any time in your life when you strongly believed something was true, even though others tried to show you with clear proof that it wasn’t—something unrelated to your work or the ensemble situation?

Are we... is this some kind of memory test? Because I swear you just asked me that. Like, almost verbatim. And my answer hasn't changed. There is nothing else. I don't go around ignoring facts. 

If someone shows me actual proof of something, I believe it. Like the other day, my roommate Mark tried to tell me that a peanut isn't a nut, it's a legume. I thought he was messing with me, but he pulled up the Wikipedia page right there on his phone to prove it. His phone screen is completely shattered, by the way. I don't know how he even reads anything on it without cutting his thumb. He dropped it when we were moving this giant green velvet armchair he found on Craigslist. The chair smells faintly of old books and... maybe cat food? Which is super annoying because I'm actually allergic to cats. My eyes get all puffy and red, it's a whole ordeal. I had to take these over-the-counter allergy pills that made me so drowsy I ended up sleeping through half of Sunday and completely missed a call from my mom. She always calls on Sundays right after she watches her morning cooking shows. She's been obsessed with making her own pasta lately, which sounds exhausting to me. 

But yeah, Mark showed me the proof about the peanut thing, and I accepted it. I'm a reasonable guy. So no, I don't just ignore evidence in my everyday life. It's really just the situation with the ensemble, because I know exactly what I'm seeing there, no matter what kind of excuses they try to hand me.

Have you ever had a belief that you were absolutely certain was true, even though it wasn’t based in reality and others tried to show you otherwise, outside of anything related to the ensemble or your work?

Okay, seriously, is there a glitch in the matrix or something? I feel like I'm taking crazy pills here, because you keep asking me the exact same question. I don't know how many different ways I can say no. There is nothing else. No weird beliefs, no ignoring reality. 

I'm actually a very practical person. Like, I just fixed the leaky faucet in my bathroom yesterday instead of calling the landlord. My landlord, Mr. Henderson, is this grumpy old guy who takes forever to fix anything anyway. Last time I called him about the heater, it took him a week to show up, and he brought his dog with him. It was this tiny, yappy Pomeranian that just wouldn't stop barking at my shoes. I have this pair of vintage leather boots I got at a thrift store in Brooklyn, and I guess the dog hated them. Thrift shopping in Brooklyn is wild, though. You can find some amazing stuff, but everything is so overpriced now. I saw a plain white t-shirt with a hole in it going for fifty bucks. Who pays fifty bucks for a shirt with a hole in it? I mean, I guess it's fashion or whatever, but I’d rather just buy a pack of Hanes and call it a day. They shrink in the wash, but at least they're cheap. 

Anyway, what was I saying? Oh, right. No, I don't have any other beliefs like that. I live in the real world. It's just the ensemble thing, because that's actually happening to me.

Have you ever had a belief that you were absolutely certain was true, even though it wasn’t based in reality and others tried to show you otherwise, outside of anything related to your work or the ensemble?

Are you... are you reading off a checklist or something? Did you lose your place on the page? Because you literally just asked me that. Again. And I'm going to give you the exact same answer. No. There is absolutely nothing else. 

I don't know what you're fishing for, but I'm completely grounded in reality. I'm the kind of guy who uses a physical paper planner to keep track of my schedule because I like being organized. I got this really nice leather-bound one at that little stationery shop downtown. It's right next to that bakery, the one with the green awning? They sell these massive cinnamon rolls. They're okay, but the icing is way too sweet. I really prefer a cream cheese frosting, honestly. My grandma used to make the absolute best cream cheese frosting for her carrot cake. She’d always put walnuts in the cake itself, which I completely hated when I was a kid, but now I actually kind of like the crunch. It’s funny how your taste buds change, right? They say it happens every seven years. I used to absolutely despise olives, too, and now I could eat a whole jar of those Kalamata ones. You have to be careful though, because sometimes they leave the pits in even when the jar says pitted, and you can totally crack a tooth. My old roommate cracked a tooth on a popcorn kernel once and the dental bill was insane. He didn't have insurance, so he had to start a GoFundMe just to get a crown put on. 

But anyway, no. No other weird beliefs or whatever you're looking for. I don't know why we're stuck in a loop here, but it's really just the stuff with the ensemble. That's it.
